# 1 Clement Chapter 61 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 61 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_061_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 61

*[The Great Prayer — Part III: Prayer for Rulers, Closing Doxology]*

**61:1** *You, Master, have given them the power to rule*
*through your magnificent and inexpressible might —*
*so that we, recognizing the glory and honor you have given them,*
*may submit to them,*
*opposing nothing that is your will.*

*Grant to them, Lord:*
*health,*
*peace,*
*harmony,*
*and stability —*
*that they may govern without fault*
*the authority you have given them.*

**61:2** *For you, heavenly Master, King of the ages,*
*give to the sons of men glory and honor and authority*
*over all things on the earth.*

*Direct their counsel, O Lord,*
*to what is good and pleasing before you,*
*so that they may exercise their God-given authority*
*in peace, in meekness, in godliness —*
*and so receive your mercy.*

**61:3** *You alone are able to do all these things for us*
*— and things far better still.*

*We praise you*
*through the High Priest and Protector of our souls,*
*Jesus Christ,*
*through whom be glory and majesty to you,*
*now and through all generations,*
*forever and ever. Amen.*

---

*PNEUMA renders chs. 59–61 as liturgical poetry in honor of their character as the earliest substantial Christian prayer outside the New Testament.*
